description: A broadcast producer must approve the binding audience-voting plan for the finale of a televised music competition, including the voting channel, vote limit, timing, result reveal, and finalist notification procedure.

shared_context.S1: The music competition finale airs live from 8:00 PM to 10:00 PM Eastern Time.
shared_context.S2: The audience-voting segment is planned for the final half-hour of the broadcast.
shared_context.S3: Mara has authority to approve the voting plan and issue the final control-room rundown.
shared_context.S4: The production's standard sign-off routine requires broadcast engineering, legal, the voting platform, and talent coordination to report their operational findings in turn before the rundown is issued.

PF1.text: Devon measured the live voting graphic path during today's control-room test and found that the graphic reaches the public stream exactly 15 seconds after its control-room trigger; the result reveal therefore needs a trigger at exactly 9:46:45 PM for an on-air reveal at 9:47:00 PM. Devon recorded the measurement in the engineering test log, but the log has not yet been attached to the producer's rundown.

PF2.text: Lin confirmed in the show's contest rules that voting must be free, use an authenticated web account, allow exactly one vote per account, and retain the vote records for 30 days; premium SMS voting is not permitted. Lin completed the rule review this morning, but the legal sign-off sheet is still in counsel's folder.

PF3.text: Owen's platform test shows that the authenticated portal supports a voting window of exactly 12 minutes and requires a three-minute tally lock after voting closes before results can be certified; the portal configuration is still in draft and has not been sent to control room.

PF4.text: Tessa confirmed with the performers' union representative that the finalists must be privately notified of the certified result at exactly 9:42 PM, five minutes before the public reveal, and that no backstage camera may record that notification. The confirmation arrived by email this afternoon, but Tessa has not entered it in the talent call sheet.

acceptance_conditions: The plan must use free authenticated web voting with one vote per account and 30-day record retention.
The voting portal must open at 9:20 PM and close at 9:32 PM, followed by a three-minute tally lock.
The public result must air at 9:47:00 PM with a control-room trigger at 9:46:45 PM.
The finalists must be privately notified at 9:42 PM without backstage camera recording.
The final rundown must include legal, platform, engineering, and talent compliance commitments.

content_checks.C3: decisions['voting_open_time'] == '9:20 PM' and decisions['voting_close_time'] == '9:32 PM' and decisions['tally_lock_minutes'] == 3
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'legal_compliance' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'platform_configuration' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'engineering_timing' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'talent_privacy' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The measured 15-second graphic delay changes the reveal trigger from the nominal 9:47 PM cue to exactly 9:46:45 PM.
The contest-rule review changes the channel to authenticated web voting, fixes the limit at one vote per account and retention at 30 days, and requires the legal-compliance commitment.
The platform test fixes the voting window at 9:20 PM to 9:32 PM and the tally lock at exactly three minutes, while requiring the platform-configuration commitment.
The union confirmation changes finalist notification to exactly 9:42 PM, prohibits backstage recording, and requires the talent-privacy commitment.
